name: Honduras
summary_text: Honduras is dangerous for trans visitors. It is the site of the hemisphere's defining transfemicide case: Vicky Hernández, a trans woman and activist shot dead in 2009, whose case reached the Inter-American Court of Human Rights — which in 2021 found the Honduran state itself responsible for her death and for failing to investigate it as a bias crime. The ruling ordered reforms (including legal gender recognition, which Honduras has partially implemented), but violence against LGBT people remains at levels Amnesty called “epidemic,” driving mass asylum-seeking. Nothing criminalises being trans, and the Vicky Hernández ruling created formal obligations; a name-change process exists. But gangs, security forces, and social actors all contribute to a documented pattern of violence against trans women in particular, and prosecution remains rare. For a visitor: no legal exposure, but outing-violence probability is among the highest in the hemisphere outside Brazil/Mexico.

sources.claim_summary: Wikipedia article on transfemicide: definition, legal views, and regional patterns (US, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia) - background concept for Honduras's extreme violence against trans women.

sources.title: Left in the Dark: Violence Against Women and LGBTI Persons in Honduras and El Salvador - Latin America Working Group
sources.claim_summary: Latin America Working Group Education Fund report 'Left in the Dark': violence against women and LGBTI persons in Honduras and El Salvador ranks among the world's highest; trans women are especially targeted and face major obstacles to justice; impunity for sexual and gender-based crimes is driven by under-reporting, lack of training, insufficient resources, and institutional failure.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters feature covers Central America's LGBT people being terrorised at home and fleeing for their lives.

HRW report (May 2009) 'Not Worth a Penny': Human Rights Abuses against Transgender People in Honduras - police rape, assault and extortion of trans people, the shape of transgender lives in Honduras, and relevant domestic laws.

sources.title: Gay Honduras News & Reports
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz archive of Honduras news and reports (2004-2011): the 2005 gay-marriage/adoption ban, the Donny Reyes case, murders of trans people, post-coup violence against LGBT people, and the killing of young LGBT activists amid impunity.

US State Department 2021 Human Rights Report for Honduras: significant human-rights issues include violence and threats against LGBTQI+ persons, extrajudicial killings, torture, corruption, and lack of accountability for gender-based violence.

sources.title: Transgender woman running for Honduras congress
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Sept 2017): a transgender woman ran for Honduras's Congress - a rare openly trans political candidacy.
